findings.description: The net task calls esp_wifi_connect() on WIFI_EVENT_STA_START but never checks whether the radio is in station mode. With the onboarding AP up (WIFI_MODE_AP, credentials still empty) esp_wifi_start() raises STA_START once, the task answers it with esp_wifi_connect(), and the driver rejects it with ESP_ERR_WIFI_MODE; the return value is ignored.
findings.evidence: app_mqtt.cpp:283-287 net_task STA_START branch calls esp_wifi_connect() with no mode check; app_mqtt.cpp:449-456 app_mqtt_ap_start uses esp_wifi_set_mode(WIFI_MODE_AP) then esp_wifi_start() only; esp_wifi_connect() returns ESP_ERR_WIFI_MODE when the station interface is not enabled.
findings.failureScenario: Boot a factory-fresh panel: the AP comes up in AP mode, STA_START fires, mqtt_net calls esp_wifi_connect(), the call fails with ESP_ERR_WIFI_MODE and nothing else happens — onboarding still works, but the failure is invisible and the driver state is misleading to anyone debugging it.
findings.suggestedChange: Call esp_wifi_connect() only when the current mode includes the station interface (track the mode alongside s_wifi_started) and log the return value.

findings.description: The Wi-Fi/IP event queue is created inside the `if (s_net_task == NULL)` guard while both esp_event_handler_register() calls pass s_net_queue unconditionally; a second init after a failed task creation registers handlers with NULL and every Wi-Fi event becomes a silent no-op.
findings.evidence: app_mqtt.cpp:744-754 (queue and task created only inside the guard, registration outside it); app_mqtt.cpp wifi_event_handler returns early when the queue is NULL.
findings.failureScenario: A second app_mqtt_init() after xTaskCreate failed leaves s_net_task NULL and s_net_queue stale or NULL: the handlers enqueue nothing, STA_START is never answered, the panel never associates and shows 'connecting' with no diagnostic.
findings.suggestedChange: Create the queue outside the guard and verify it before registering the handlers.

findings.description: The factory reset remains a 10 s hold of the single front button rather than the spec's SET+MODE combination.
findings.evidence: app_logic.cpp:375-376 registers COMBO_ARM_MS on handles[0]; on_set_arm arms the 10 s NVS wipe.
findings.failureScenario: A finger resting on the front button for 10 s erases Wi-Fi, broker and room topics without a second confirming button.
findings.suggestedChange: Keep the spec combination or require a second confirmation inside the countdown.

notes: No MDNS symbol exists in the generated sdkconfig.h (no mdns Kconfig is sourced), so CONFIG_MDNS_TASK_STACK_SIZE has no effect; the writer acknowledged this and the last 2.5-minute idle run did not reproduce the mdns abort, so the exposure is unproven and must be re-checked on hardware.

The commissioned-reboot crash changed shape (now a CPU cache fault inside the Wi-Fi driver at an unmapped PC); the new fix (start the station from mqtt_net, radio restarted in STA mode after commissioning instead of APSTA) has not been exercised yet.
The onboarding AP now runs in AP mode only, so a panel is either an access point or a station, never both.
Standing deviations: plain-MQTT default broker, empty-payload TRV poll, single-button factory reset, three-number voice vocabulary.

report.summary: The reboot crash is addressed in code (station start moved to mqtt_net, commissioning restarts the radio in STA mode instead of APSTA) and builds clean, but it has not been re-tested; two new info notes (esp_wifi_connect on STA_START without a mode check, queue created under a conditional guard) and the acknowledged no-op mdns stack line remain.
